title: Reasoning Models
description: A visual introduction to reasoning models: reasoning steps, compute budgets, the five questions covered in the series, and tradeoffs between quality, cost, latency and risk.

provenance.timing_basis: Candidate scene/cue boundaries compared with decoded approved media; this is not identification of the renderer source.
provenance.upload_date_basis: Observed completion of production deploy-pages step in workflow 35514981780; first-publication time of these exact bytes may be earlier.

chapters.name: Reasoning is a process.

cues.text: A complex problem can be broken into steps.
Those steps consume time and compute.

visual_description: The illustrative multiplication 17 × 6 is split into 10 × 6 and 7 × 6: 60 + 42 = 102. An answer of 104 is marked incorrect. The grid represents the calculation being broken down, not a benchmark result.

chapters.name: The budget is also a choice.

cues.text: At inference time, you can spend more steps, samples, verification or tool interactions.
On some tasks that can improve the answer, but it also increases cost and latency.

visual_description: Twelve units of compute are allocated to steps, samples and verification. This is an illustrative allocation: it shows that a budget can be distributed in different ways, not that one allocation is universally optimal.

chapters.name: One series, five questions.

cues.text: First: what reasoning means for an LLM.
Third: how to use more inference-time compute.
Fourth: what happens to latency and streaming.
Fifth: when more reasoning introduces new risks.

visual_description: The map connects reasoning to five questions: what it means, how it fails, how to use test-time compute, what happens to latency, and what risks it introduces. Quality, cost and time are shown as related decisions.

chapters.name: Thinking longer is not free.

cues.text: More reasoning can improve quality on suitable tasks.
It also consumes time, compute and money.
And it can introduce overthinking, errors or new attack surfaces.

visual_description: A triangle connects quality, cost and latency, and risk around the task. This is a qualitative comparison: position does not represent a score or a performance measurement.
